newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt up with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt up with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were higher in late trade, bolstered by a rally in the U.S. Treasury market and strong demand for Argentina's upcoming $2.0 billion global bond issue, emerging market traders said.

"The U.S. Treasury market is supporting the Brady market," said one market source, who noted that testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to the Senate Budget Committee earlier today also helped to push prices higher.
At 1600 EST/2100 GMT, Argentine discount bonds AR425C23=RR were 7/8 firmer at 80-5/8 bid and the country's FRBs ARFLC05=RR were 3/4 firmer at 89-3/4 bid.
Emerging market trading sources attributed the gains in Argentine paper to the extremely good demand for its 20-year global bond, which is expected to be priced Wednesday.

"There is a lot of hype in the market regarding the Argentine deal. It is almost four times oversubsrcibed. There is demand for about $7.0 billion," said one emerging markets trader at a large U.S. investment firm.
"Clearly with that much demand it makes Argentina look extrememly cheap and I think you are just seeing the market trade up on that," the trader added.
Seperately, Argentine Treasury Secretary Pablo Guidotti told reporters in Buenos Aires that the $2.0 billion global bond had been three times oversubscribed.
Market sources said the fact that the global bond will have a 20-year maturity also boosted investor confidence.
"It's good news that it will be 20-year bond because it will take some pressure out of the short end of the curve," said another market source.
In the broader sector of the market, Mexican pars MX625L19=RR were one percentage point higher at 75-1/4 bid and Brazilian "C" bonds were 3/4 firmer at 76-3/8 bid.
Traders said continued buying by non-traditional emerging market investors also supported the market.
"We continue to see a lot of new money flowing in. There is a lot of crossover buying," said a trading source who noted that here was absolutely no selling by clients.
Ecuadoran Bradys also continued higher despite growing uncertainty over whether the convertability law will be approved by the country's Congress.
"On a relative value basis, people are forced to buy Ecuador despite the fundamentals," said a trader.
Ecuadoran PDI bonds ECPDI=RR were one percentage higher at 65-3/8 bid.
Elsewhere, Russian Vnesheconombank loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were unchanged 79-3/4 while Bulgarian FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were 7/8 firmer at 39-1/4.
